package_info.package_manager: N/A (custom malware, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: DinodasRAT is a custom multi-platform backdoor malware specifically designed to target Linux systems. It achieves persistence, collects detailed system and user information, and establishes encrypted command-and-control (C2) communication for data exfiltration and remote espionage. Its core behaviors—unauthorized access, covert data theft, and remote command execution—are definitive hallmarks of malicious software.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (immediately upon execution of the malware binary)
execution_context.file_location: main malware binary (e.g., /usr/bin/dinodas or similar location after installation)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
system_info = collect_system_info()
unique_id = hash(system_info)
send_to_c2(unique_id, system_info)
malicious_snippets.code_language: python (pseudocode, actual malware likely C/C++ or Go)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects detailed system and user information, generates a unique identifier for the infected machine, and transmits this data to a remote command-and-control server, enabling victim profiling and targeted espionage.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The collection of comprehensive system and user information followed by exfiltration to an external server is a classic reconnaissance and victim identification tactic used by advanced malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not silently collect and transmit detailed system information to unknown external servers without explicit user consent or a clear, transparent purpose.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise asset management or monitoring tools may collect system information, but they do so with user or administrator awareness and only transmit data to trusted, documented endpoints.
key_indicators: Automated collection of system and user information at process startup
Generation of unique host identifiers based on system attributes
Outbound network communication to hardcoded or suspicious C2 infrastructure

execution_context.trigger: runtime (during initial execution, persistence setup phase)
execution_context.file_location: init scripts (e.g., /etc/init.d/, systemd service files such as /etc/systemd/system/dinodas.service, or crontab entries)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
install_persistence()
# e.g., create systemd service or cron job to relaunch malware on boot
malicious_snippets.code_language: shell (pseudocode, actual implementation may use shell commands or direct file manipulation in C/C++)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code installs persistence mechanisms by creating or modifying system startup scripts, systemd service files, or scheduled cron jobs to ensure the malware binary is automatically relaunched after system reboots.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unauthorized modification of system startup mechanisms to ensure malware persistence is a well-established technique for maintaining long-term access to compromised systems.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not silently install persistence mechanisms or alter system startup files without explicit user approval and a legitimate operational need.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System management or update tools may install services or scheduled tasks, but only with user or administrator approval and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Creation or modification of systemd service files referencing unknown or suspicious binaries
Unauthorized changes to /etc/init.d/ scripts or crontab entries
Persistence mechanisms referencing non-standard or undocumented binaries

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after initial beacon to C2, during ongoing operation)
execution_context.file_location: main malware binary (network communication and command execution routines)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
connect_to_c2()
while True:
    command = receive_command()
    execute_command(command)
    send_results_to_c2()
malicious_snippets.code_language: python (pseudocode, actual malware likely C/C++ or Go)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware establishes a persistent connection to a remote command-and-control server, receives attacker-issued commands, executes them on the infected host, and exfiltrates the results, enabling covert remote control and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Maintaining a persistent C2 connection and executing arbitrary remote commands are core backdoor behaviors, providing attackers with full control over the compromised system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not establish covert, persistent connections to unknown external servers for the purpose of executing arbitrary commands received over the network.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools may provide similar functionality, but only when installed with user or administrator knowledge and configured to connect to trusted, documented infrastructure.
key_indicators: Persistent outbound connections to suspicious or unlisted domains/IPs
Ability to receive and execute arbitrary commands from a remote server
Exfiltration of command execution results to external infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Malware binary is executed on the target Linux system, initiating the infection process.
attack_chain.leads_to: System information collection and installation of persistence mechanisms

attack_chain.action: Malware collects detailed system and user information, generates a unique identifier, and transmits this data to the C2 server.
Malware installs persistence mechanisms by modifying system startup scripts, systemd service files, or cron jobs to ensure automatic relaunch after reboot.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ensures continued access and re-infection after system restarts

attack_chain.action: Malware establishes persistent C2 communication, receives and executes attacker commands, and exfiltrates results to the remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing remote control, data exfiltration, and espionage

behavioral_signatures: Automated collection and outbound transmission of system and user information at process startup
Creation or modification of systemd service files, init scripts, or cron jobs referencing unknown or suspicious binaries
Persistent outbound connections to suspicious or unlisted domains/IPs, especially shortly after process startup
Processes executing arbitrary commands received from network-based C2 infrastructure
file_indicators: Unknown or recently created binaries in /usr/bin/, /usr/local/bin/, or /tmp/
New or modified systemd service files (e.g., /etc/systemd/system/dinodas.service) referencing non-standard binaries
Unexpected or unauthorized entries in crontab or /etc/init.d/ that reference unfamiliar executables
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known DinodasRAT C2 domains or IP addresses as identified in threat intelligence feeds
Unusual beaconing patterns to external servers on non-standard ports, especially immediately after process startup
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the creation or modification of system binaries and persistence mechanisms (systemd, cron, init scripts) referencing unknown executables. Correlate automated system information collection and outbound network activity at process startup. Detect persistent outbound connections to suspicious or unlisted domains/IPs, and alert on processes executing commands received from network sources. Leverage threat intelligence to block or alert on known DinodasRAT C2 infrastructure.
